sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: ML for Beginners is a free 12-week, 26-lesson course from Microsoft that teaches classic machine learning, mainly with Scikit-learn. Each lesson uses real data from different parts of the world and includes quizzes and assignments.
sixtySeconds.problem: Many machine learning resources jump straight into deep learning or assume a strong maths background. This curriculum builds up classic techniques like regression, classification and clustering step by step through projects.
whoFor: Students and teachers wanting a ready-made curriculum
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a structured, project-based introduction to classic ML that's free and well supported. It intentionally avoids deep learning, which Microsoft covers in a separate AI for Beginners course.
requirements: Python (or GitHub Codespaces in the browser)
Git and a GitHub account to fork the repo

overview: The curriculum spans 12 weeks and 26 lessons on classic machine learning, primarily using Scikit-learn and avoiding deep learning. Lessons travel around the world, applying techniques to data from many regions.

Each lesson includes a pre-lecture quiz, written instructions, a solution, an assignment and a post-lecture quiz. Students are encouraged to build the projects from understanding rather than running the solution code, which lives in each lesson's solution folder.

You can fork and clone the repository, or open it in GitHub Codespaces to skip local Python setup. A sparse clone skips the 50+ translations to speed up the download, and a troubleshooting guide covers setup issues.

steps.title: Clone without translations
steps.code:
git clone --filter=blob:none --sparse https://github.com/microsoft/ML-For-Beginners.git
cd ML-For-Beginners
git sparse-checkout set --no-cone '/*' '!translations' '!translated_images'
